packs.title: Gardens and Riverlines
packs.promise: Find a bronze tree, a palace frame and a bridge line that shifts.

q.s: Find a large frame, a small opening and a reflected line.
st: Find a pair of columns that frames a dark opening, a smaller window above and a long horizontal line along the palace or its reflection.
Mark each at a different scale: tall frame, small opening, long line. A reflection is optional; another visible building edge works equally well.
Save your three observations. A short written description earns the same credit as a sketch.

q.s: Build three small panels from an outdoor theatre.
st: Choose one curved edge, one upright column and one open space between the theatre’s pale architectural forms.
Make three original small panels on paper or in words: let the curve start the first, the upright start the second and the gap start the third.
Arrange your panels into a miniature stage of your own and give it a short title. Keep all marks on your own paper or device.

q.s: Turn a tall window and brick edges into a small original pattern.
st: Find one tall window shape, one repeated brick edge and one long chimney outline in the historic exterior.
Make three original marks or short shape descriptions, then repeat them twice in a small pattern on your own paper or device.
Choose a different order for the second repeat and save the pattern you prefer. Do not copy signs or draw on buildings or paving.

packs.title: Colourlines and Quiet Corners
packs.promise: Find Warsaw in a coloured facade, a changing frame and a quiet garden detail.

q.s: Collect three small details from the Old Town Market Square.
st: Choose an open edge of the Market Square where you can see several townhouse fronts without blocking cafe seating or entrances.
Collect three visible details: a window shape, a roofline detail and a change of facade colour.
Give each detail a short name that would help you find it again. Link each name to its position on the row.
Choose the detail you would keep if your collection could contain only one thing, and explain your choice.

q.s: Let the Royal Castle’s facade start two lines of your own.
st: Choose a comfortable public spot in Castle Square with a view of the Royal Castle. Leave entrances and walking routes clear.
Find one long horizontal line along the facade and one upward line on the central clock tower.
Write two short original lines: let the first travel sideways and the second rise. Start with the shapes you can actually see.
Choose one word in either line to change, then save the version you prefer.

q.s: Write a small connection between a facade and a tree.
st: Find a comfortable stopping place on the public pavement with a view of street trees and a neighbouring facade.
Choose a colour on the building and a contrasting colour in a leaf, tree shadow or patch of sky beside it.
Write one original sentence that brings the two colours together. Use a comparison or a tiny imagined movement.
Read it silently, replace one word if you like and save the sentence with the two details that began it.
